My niece has just become of driving age and she will be visiting me this summer. She desperately wants a car, but her school drving instructor called her "a menace on the road". Is there a simulator game that accurately simulates real drving conditions and demonstrates safety? I have a fairly decent three screen gaming PC and I don't mind constructing a simulator rig with a wheel and pedals. Any ideas what software to use?

Edit: Euro Truck Simulator has been suggested and it looks like it probably would work for my purposes. I also found a promising open source solution from Germany, OpenDS.
Do you have any recommendations for a non-racing driving simulator to teach real-world driving skills?

I'm gonna go 50/50 with the response:

Grand Theft Auto (because duh)

L.A. Noire (really cool game where you solve murders as a detective, but the driving in the game actually scolds you for running red lights and hitting people (because you're a cop)

Give it a try first, play the story line and see if it's appropriate or whatever, or you could just have a save that is about a third of the way through the game which will then open up the whole map to drive around on. Plus it takes place in LA and there are a lot of sights and attractions that are in the game that are in real life so that's cool!
L.A. Noire probably has the worst driving mechanics of any Rockstar published game and any GTA-like game ever released. It's that bad. A shame, because the collection of cars was awesome.

Unfortunately unless you're willing to spend a small fortune on equipment, the car experience will not translate well to a simulator. The biggest problem becomes that you can't feel the forces of the car, and the display doesn't force you to do things like checking your blind spots, or looking behind you when you back up. Essentially, your awareness becomes fixed on only what the game camera shows you which is not enough.

If you want your daughter to get better on the road, she needs to keep driving a real car supervised. This is the only way she's going to get a feel for the car, the road, and gain an awareness of what is going on around her. Don't be too discouraged if she doesn't master these skills right away - some people need to get older and more sure of themselves before they properly learn this set of skills.

If driving is too much, try other activities that build confidence and promote situational awareness.

Cyclist drafting behind a truck at 50+ mph

I did such things quite often, cycling to and from highschool, and still do. It's surprisingly easy, once you learn to time your acceleration properly. A couple months ago I caught a scooter's draft, cycling 50kph for a long time. On a side note, catching trams in Amsterdam is a lot of fun, seeing tourists suddenly getting frantic wanting to take pics.

50+mph though is something else. This dude must have his balls to the wall, and maybe all over the tarmac one day...

Edit, cause the more the merrier: to catch the draft, aim for relatively slow moving vehicles, which you know will speed up shortly after. Stay as close as you can/dare, keeping an eye out for sudden braking. Know the road, and you can try it quite safely.

To catch a tram (as a tourist: don't), really it's the same: find a tram slowly accelerating and latch on to the side. There're some rounded off corners you can hold on to. It will take you up to 50kph in a couple seconds. Again, know the road ahead.
